content.text: All exclusivity in this agreement runs in our favour; nothing restricts AbbVie's freedom to source or develop elsewhere.

input.quote: 5.8.1 Harpoon shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to (a) directly or indirectly, develop, commercialize or otherwise exploit any Competing Product in any country or other jurisdiction in the Territory, or (b) license, authorize, appoint, or otherwise enable any Third Party to directly or indirectly, develop, commercialize or otherwise exploit any Competing Product in any country or other jurisdiction in the Territory, except, in each case ((a) and (b)), as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement.
input.rationale: The rule's preferred position is met: no exclusivity, sole-supplier or non-procurement covenant binds AbbVie anywhere in the Agreement. The entire exclusivity architecture runs in our favour — Section 5.8.1 is a Competing Product non-compete imposed on Harpoon and its Affiliates only; Sections 5.1.3(a)-(b) grant AbbVie exclusive licences and rights of reference (including against Harpoon); Section 5.6.1 subjects Harpoon's retained rights to Section 5.8; and Section 7.1.2 expressly preserves "in the case of Harpoon, its exclusivity obligations hereunder" as a limit on Harpoon's, not AbbVie's, exploitation of Joint IP. Conversely, AbbVie's freedom of action is affirmatively protected: Section 5.2 grants Harpoon only a non-exclusive, narrow licence; Sections 5.3, 5.4 and 5.5 give AbbVie sole-discretion rights to sublicense through multiple tiers, appoint distributors and co-promote with any Third Party; and Section 5.9.2 gives AbbVie the first right to take Third Party in-licences. A search for sole-supplier, requirements, exclusive-supply and "shall not develop" style restrictions returned nothing binding AbbVie, and the only "AbbVie shall not" provisions concern records inspection, royalty reductions and settlement conduct — none restricting sourcing. Section 5.8.2's Acquisition/Change of Control carve-outs narrow Harpoon's own covenant and additionally confer termination and information-cut-off rights on AbbVie, so they benefit us. Per the detection guidance, exclusivity granted to the Customer is acceptable and is not a deviation; no redline is warranted.
